patterns_found.name: I/O hole subtraction for accurate computation timing

gotchas.text: Newton fraction blowup: numeric::root(power=2, iter) creates million-bit integers at iter=20. Keep iter <= 12. sqrt(2) uses iter=10 which is safe.
pi computation uses a for(;;) convergence loop that may take many iterations — the entire loop is one benchmark block, not per-iteration timing.
Header-only globals in id.hpp/ii.hpp cause multi-TU linker errors. main.cpp is a single TU — safe.
normalize(3) semantics: bit1=trim trailing zero bits, bit2=GCD reduce. Important for understanding post-computation normalization in timed blocks.

prior_decisions.decision: Flat JSON format {name: nanos} for baseline — no nested structure
rationale: Simplest hand-written parser (no recursion, no nesting)
Easily extensible later by adding new keys at the same level

prior_decisions.decision: Table columns show milliseconds (ms) not nanoseconds
rationale: Milliseconds are more readable for human scanning
Nanos stored internally for precision; converted to ms for display

prior_decisions.decision: --benchmark-json output goes to stdout after table, not a separate file
rationale: Users can redirect with > to capture JSON separately
Backward compatibility for any scripts consuming the raw stats
